notes:
I couldn't write these notes. I don't have any research results to work from: my tool for opening web pages was cut off before it fetched a single page, and I can't make more calls this turn.

You asked me to report only what the pages actually say, with a URL for every point, and to leave out anything I couldn't find. Since I read nothing, there's nothing I can honestly report. Writing notes on Psalm 16 from memory and attaching URLs I never opened would break your rules, so I haven't done it.

If you ask again in a new turn, I'll start by reading the main verse-by-verse sources:
- enduringword.com/bible-commentary/psalm-16/
- The Gill, Ellicott and Pulpit Commentary pages on biblehub.com for Psalms 16
- The Psalm 16 commentary on preceptaustin.org

Then I'd fill in the other parts:
- **Where Protestant traditions differ:** Spurgeon's *Treasury of David* (spurgeon.org or ccel.org), Wesley's Notes (wesley.nnu.edu), the Reformed sites (Ligonier, The Gospel Coalition, Desiring God) and Lutheran pages (lcms.org, 1517.org). The likely focus is v. 10 ("Holy One… decay"), which Acts 2 and 13 apply to Christ's resurrection, and whether verses 9–11 are about David, Christ, or both.
- **Other views:** the netbible.org notes for modern scholarship (for example on "saints" in v. 3, "libations" in v. 4 and "Sheol" in v. 10), and the Catholic and Orthodox readings on newadvent.org, catholic.com and oca.org. Those sites may list it as Psalm 15, because their older Bibles number the Psalms differently.

To fit within the limits, I'd open several pages per call and print only the parts I need.
